stops.note: a jelly made from red seaweed, used in cooking across the Malay world and in Java under Dutch rule
Fanny Hesse, who knew agar jelly from a Dutch neighbour who had lived in Java, suggested it to Robert Koch's lab in Berlin as a solid medium for growing bacteria
spread with Koch's methods; Julius Petri's shallow dish of 1887 was designed to hold it

current_meaning: a gel from red seaweed used in food and to grow microbes
